title: Route-aware Track 1 safety exit reporting before paper

verdicts.safety_exit_legacy_trade_log_blocker: CLOSED in code and under test; NOT yet live (scheduler pid 48604 still holds this morning's argv)

q1_current_safety_exit_write_path.why_stop_repair_is_a_writer: B3 runs inside FuturesRunner.__init__; a matched stop is booked and a CLOSE row written. The hardcoded path was added 2026-08-17 after a max-hold close moved equity and left the log untouched.

q2_destination.why_separate_file: paper_evidence_reader aggregates the whole trade log and splits on nothing (measured). The route's own PAPER_OUTPUT_POLICY already said 'SEPARATE file until paper_evidence_reader can split on route'.
q2_destination.why_under_track1_runtime_root: the five sibling per-route files and every Track 1 reader already live there
q2_destination.reader_collision_check: every Track 1 runtime reader targets a named subdirectory with an explicit glob; nothing enumerates the runtime root. The new file is invisible to all.

contract.no_argument: trade_log.jsonl, byte for byte; no probe, no mkdir, no touch
contract.trade_log_path_given: used, and proven writable now or the job exits 1
contract.route_given: every row this run writes carries route=R

q3_cli_design.why_not_inferred: a caller who changed the book but not the log would silently keep writing legacy's file
q3_cli_design.probe_ordering: before the positions check, because both scripts return early when the book is absent and in shadow that is every run
q3_cli_design.probe_kind: append-open of the real file (exactly what the writer does), not a permission bit on the directory
q3_cli_design.probe_side_effect: creates the file empty on first success, so 'never swept' and 'swept, closed nothing' are distinguishable

q5_safety_semantics.how_tests_avoid_orders: IBKRBroker class and FuturesRunner both replaced before construction; max-hold additionally run with --dry-run

q6_reporting_compatibility.mechanism: FuturesRunner(route=None) optional kwarg, last in the signature; _append_trade_raw uses setdefault so a caller that already named its route wins

tag_value_deviates_from_brief.reason: matches the route field every other Track 1 artefact already carries (slot_timing, window_coverage, runner events, live state)

q7_readiness_gates.closed_here: Track 1 safety exits write the legacy trade log

not_yet_live.entry_point_changes: already live — each safety job is a fresh subprocess importing current source
not_yet_live.scheduler_argv: NOT live — built inside the running scheduler process, pid 48604, started 01:07 ET today
not_yet_live.consequence: until a restart, Track 1 safety jobs are still invoked with no destination and no route and would still write the legacy log

live_positions_track1_json.consequence: both Track 1 safety jobs stop taking their early return and will acquire the lock and connect to IBKR on every sweep

tests.two_layer_composition: which destination the SCRIPT chooses (main() with broker and FuturesRunner replaced) + what the RUNNER's real writer does with it (FuturesRunner._append_trade on an object.__new__ instance, so B3/B4 never run)

mutations.method: source-level edits run in a SUBPROCESS; in-process patching cannot express scheduler wiring or statement ordering
harness_defects_found_and_fixed: restore compared file BYTES to re-encoded TEXT — always fails in a CRLF repo, aborted the sweep mid-run
two anchors whose indentation made them suffixes of a second line, matching twice — reported as harness-broken, then pinned
